notes.decision: Translated as 'the upper side' (variant of ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲧⲉ in glossary, the upper region) rather than 'the chosen one' (the Zarathustra epithet). The parallelism with ⲡⲥⲁⲙⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ 'the lower side' (line 7) and the spatial-correspondential context (Fathers above gazing down at lower realm) confirms this reading. The orthography ⲥⲁⲧⲧ for ⲥⲁⲛⲧⲧⲉ shows further contraction.
Translated as 'icon' (= Greek εἰκών). Lycopolitan ⲁⲕⲟⲛ for εἰκών with prosthetic ϩ- for the rough breathing. Same lexeme appears in line 13 paired with ⲍⲁⲓ̈ⲃⲉⲥ 'shadow' confirming 'image/icon' sense.

Line 16 contains physically-present text whose meaning resists confident parsing. ⲁⲣⲡⲉ may be a defective/dialectal form (possibly related to ⲁⲣⲡⲉⲓ 'reach/extend' or ⲣ̄ⲡⲉ 'be heavy'); ⲕⲙⲧ[ⲟ] likely completes ⲕⲙⲧⲟ 'earthquake/disturbance' (in glossary); ⲱⲃⲉ may be the end of a longer word in the lost portion. Kept untranslated in English as a placeholder rendering, with notes for human review.

Translated 'stretched downward.' ⲥⲣⲁⲕⲉ is likely related to ⲥⲱⲣ 'spread' or ⲥⲱⲣⲕ̄ 'pull, draw' — the shadow is stretched/extended down upon the earth even as the body that casts it hangs upward (line 21). The cosmological-correspondential point: the cosmic body has come up out of the Deep, and its 'shadow' extends downward in the lower world.

Greek προγνώστης 'foreknower' (one who knows in advance). The Coptic spelling has ⲣⲛ for ⲅⲛ (assimilation/dialectal). Translated 'foreknower' to preserve the verbal-prefixed sense ('first-knower') which the chapter explicitly explicates in line 33-34 with ⲣ̄ϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛⲣⲉϩⲥⲁⲩⲛⲉ 'first-know.' Avoided generic 'prophet' which loses the morpheme structure.

Reads as a Lycopolitan reduplicated/extended form of ⲁⲙⲁϩⲧⲉ 'grasp, seize, hold,' parallel to the simpler ⲙⲁϩⲣ̄ in line 24 of the chapter heading. Translated 'grasp them' to match the heading's identical verb. The reduplication may intensify ('firmly grasp / take possession of').

Greek κατά + Lycopolitan ⲣⲁⲓ̈ (1sg suffix on prepositional ⲣⲁ⸗) = 'according to me / as I see it.' The elect is offering his interpretive perspective to the apostle, asking the question while proposing his own understanding of how the Mind of Light's grasp works. Standard Coptic 'κατὰ + suffix' construction.
